paragraphs: Bullard makes protective equipment worn on the job: hard hats, face shields, respirators, fire helmets and thermal imaging cameras. Fire departments are among the buyers, taking helmets for protection and thermal imagers as a second set of eyes in smoke.

The respiratory line serves healthcare, pharmaceutical and industrial settings where workers face pathogens, particulates, mist, vapors and sprays. Abrasive blasting gets its own complete systems, bundling a helmet with airline hose, climate control and a carbon monoxide monitor. Buyers configure gear on the site and get a suggested retail price to take to a distributor.

The company traces its line of work back to designing the first hard hat in 1919, and has been in blasting equipment for over half a century. It sells through channel partners around the world rather than direct, and lists its address in Cynthiana, Kentucky.
